-- Gaming Mode on NVIDIA + 4K TV: the screen sometimes showed torn bands and
-- stale blocks of earlier frames (scanout racing the GPU). Turn off gamescope's
-- explicit-sync path on the DRM backend so it waits for frames the old way.
gamescope.convars.drm_debug_disable_explicit_sync.value = true
(warn or print)("50-nvidia-tv-fix: drm_debug_disable_explicit_sync = " .. tostring(gamescope.convars.drm_debug_disable_explicit_sync.value))

-- GBM scan-out buffers (only exists in GBM-patched gamescope builds; stock ignores this).
-- NVIDIA can't scan out non-contiguous memory; Vulkan-allocated 4K buffers sometimes are.
local gbm = gamescope.convars.drm_gbm_scanout
if gbm then
    gbm.value = true
    ;(warn or print)("50-nvidia-tv-fix: drm_gbm_scanout = " .. tostring(gbm.value))
end

read.~/.local/bin/gaming-mode-cycle:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Repeatedly enter Gaming Mode so torn/clean starts can be watched and reported.
#   gaming-mode-cycle [rounds=5] [seconds-per-round=25] [delays...]
#   e.g. gaming-mode-cycle 12 25 0 4 8 15   # rotate start delays 0,4,8,15 s per round
# With delays given, each round's start delay is set before it starts and the
# previous delay is restored at the end (the diag index logs delay= per session).
# GAMING_MODE_CYCLE_ARGS="none|--disable-color-management" rotates extra gamescope
# flags per round the same way ('|'-separated, 'none' = no extra flags).
# Run from the desktop. Each round is numbered in the diag index
# (~/.local/state/gaming-mode-diag/index.log) so "3 bad" maps to a log.
# After the last round it returns to the desktop.
rounds=${1:-5}; hold=${2:-25}; shift 2 2>/dev/null || shift $#; delays=("$@")
here="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
IFS='|' read -r -a argsets <<< "${GAMING_MODE_CYCLE_ARGS:-}"
set_delay() {  # set_delay <round>: pick this round's delay from the list
    [ ${#delays[@]} -gt 0 ] && "$here/gaming-mode-delay" "${delays[$(( ($1 - 1) % ${#delays[@]} ))]}" >/dev/null
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    [ ${#argsets[@]} -gt 0 ] && "$here/gaming-mode-extra-args" ${argsets[$(( ($1 - 1) % ${#argsets[@]} ))]} >/dev/null
    return 0
}
idx="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/gaming-mode-diag/index.log"
flag="$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/easy-switch-gamescope-restart"
active() { systemctl --user is-active --quiet gamescope-session.service; }
wait_for() {  # wait_for up|down <timeout>
    for _ in $(seq 1 "$2"); do
        if [ "$1" = up ]; then active && return 0; else active || return 0; fi
        sleep 1
    done
    return 1
}

# Detach from the desktop session: it gets logged out on the first switch.
if [ -z "$GAMING_MODE_CYCLE_DETACHED" ]; then
    exec systemd-run --user --collect --unit="gaming-mode-cycle-$(date +%H%M%S)" \
        --setenv=GAMING_MODE_CYCLE_DETACHED=1 --setenv=XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR" \
        --setenv=GAMING_MODE_CYCLE_ARGS="${GAMING_MODE_CYCLE_ARGS:-}" \
        "$(readlink -f "$0")" "$rounds" "$hold" "$@"
fi

orig_delay=$("$here/gaming-mode-delay"); orig_args=$("$here/gaming-mode-extra-args")
echo "$(date '+%F %T') CYCLE start: $rounds rounds x ${hold}s, delays: ${delays[*]:-unchanged ($orig_delay)}, args: ${GAMING_MODE_CYCLE_ARGS:-unchanged ($orig_args)}" >> "$idx"
set_delay 1
active || steamos-session-select gamescope
for i in $(seq 1 "$rounds"); do
    if ! wait_for up 120; then echo "$(date '+%F %T') CYCLE round $i: Gaming Mode never started, stopping" >> "$idx"; exit 1; fi
    echo "$(date '+%F %T') CYCLE round $i of $rounds" >> "$idx"
    sleep "$hold"
    [ "$i" -lt "$rounds" ] && { set_delay $((i + 1)); touch "$flag"; }   # relog straight back into Gaming Mode
    systemctl --user --no-block stop gamescope-session.target
    wait_for down 60
done
[ ${#delays[@]} -gt 0 ] && "$here/gaming-mode-delay" "$orig_delay" >/dev/null
# shellcheck disable=SC2086
[ ${#argsets[@]} -gt 0 ] && "$here/gaming-mode-extra-args" $orig_args >/dev/null
echo "$(date '+%F %T') CYCLE done" >> "$idx"
read.~/.local/bin/gaming-mode-delay:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Show or set the Gaming Mode start delay (NVIDIA TV testing).
#   gaming-mode-delay        # print current seconds
#   gaming-mode-delay 8      # wait 8 s before gamescope starts (0 = off)
# Takes effect on the next Gaming Mode start; no reload needed.
f="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/gaming-mode/start-delay.env"
if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    sed -n 's/^GAMING_MODE_START_DELAY=//p' "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep . || echo 0
    exit 0
fi
[[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [ "$1" -le 60 ] || { echo "usage: gaming-mode-delay <0-60>" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$f")"
echo "GAMING_MODE_START_DELAY=$1" > "$f"
echo "start delay: $1 s"
read.~/.local/bin/gaming-mode-diag:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Snapshot display state for each Gaming Mode start, to compare torn vs clean sessions.
# Started by gaming-mode-diag.service (WantedBy=gamescope-session.target).
#   logs:   ~/.local/state/gaming-mode-diag/<start-time>.log
#   index:  ~/.local/state/gaming-mode-diag/index.log   (one line per session + marks)
# Mark a session:  gaming-mode-diag mark bad|good ["note"]   (marks the newest session)
dir="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/gaming-mode-diag"
mkdir -p "$dir"

if [ "$1" = mark ]; then
    latest=$(ls -1t "$dir"/2*.log 2>/dev/null | head -1)
    [ -n "$latest" ] || { echo "no sessions logged yet" >&2; exit 1; }
    line="$(date +%T) MARK $2 ${3:-} -> $(basename "$latest")"
    echo "$line" >> "$latest"; echo "$line" >> "$dir/index.log"; echo "$line"
    exit 0
fi

start_epoch=$(date +%s)
start_iso=$(date '+%F %T')
log="$dir/$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log"
connector=$(sed -n 's/^OUTPUT_CONNECTOR=\([^,]*\).*/\1/p' "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/easy-switch/gamescope.env" 2>/dev/null)

props() {   # connector properties as the driver currently has them
    modetest -M nvidia-drm -c 2>/dev/null | awk -v c="$1" '$0 ~ c {f=1} f && /^[0-9]+\t/ && $0 !~ c {f=0} f' \
        | awk '/^\t[0-9]+ [^:]+:$/ {sub(/^\t[0-9]+ /,""); name=$0; next}
               /^\t\tvalue:/ && name ~ /Colorspace|HDR_OUTPUT_METADATA|dithering|vrr_capable|link-status|DPMS/ {
                   v=$0; sub(/^\t\tvalue:/,"",v); printf "  %s %s\n", name, (v==""?"(blob)":v); blob=(v==""); if(!blob) name=""; next}
               blob && /^\t\t\t[0-9a-f]+$/ {printf "    %s\n", $1; next}
               blob && !/^\t\t\t/ {blob=0; name=""}'
}
snap() {   # snap <label> <tag>
    echo "=== snapshot +$(( $(date +%s) - start_epoch ))s ($1) ==="
    echo "-- connectors (enabled):"; for d in /sys/class/drm/card*-*; do printf '  %s %s %s\n' "${d##*/}" "$(cat "$d/status")" "$(cat "$d/enabled")"; done
    [ -n "$connector" ] && { echo "-- $connector properties:"; props "$connector"; }
    echo "-- active CRTC modes:"; modetest -M nvidia-drm -p 2>/dev/null | awk '/^CRTCs:/{f=1} /^Planes:/{f=0} f' | grep -E "^[0-9]|#[0-9]" | head -6
    # What gamescope itself composited: torn here = gamescope rendering; clean here
    # while the TV is torn = scanout/driver side.
    shot="${log%.log}-$2.png"
    if [ -n "$GAMESCOPE_WAYLAND_DISPLAY" ] && gamescopectl screenshot "$shot" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        sleep 1; [ -s "$shot" ] && echo "-- screenshot: $shot" || echo "-- screenshot: requested, not written"
    else
        echo "-- screenshot: gamescopectl failed"
    fi
    [ -s "$link" ] && echo "-- TV link (SCDC): $(tail -1 "$link")"
    echo "-- kernel HDMI infoframes / errors since start:"
    journalctl -k --since "$start_iso" --no-pager -o short-precise 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "infoframe|nvidia|drm|segfault" | grep -v UFW | tail -15
}

delay=$("$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"/gaming-mode-delay 2>/dev/null || echo "?")
xargs_=$("$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"/gaming-mode-extra-args 2>/dev/null || echo "?")
echo "$(date -d "@$start_epoch" '+%F %T') session $(basename "$log") screen=${connector:-?} delay=${delay}s args=${xargs_// /,}" >> "$dir/index.log"
# TV-side HDMI link health (SCDC) for the whole session, every 2 s -> <session>-link.log
link="${log%.log}-link.log"
hdmi_link="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/gaming-mode-hdmi-link"
case "$connector" in HDMI-*) GAMING_MODE_HDMI_CONNECTOR="$connector" "$hdmi_link" watch 2 > "$link" 2>&1 & ;; esac
link_verdict() {   # summarise the link log so far: clean | BAD(<reasons>)
    # The TV's error counters are not reliably cleared on read (LG keeps the count from link
    # bring-up), so only errors that *grow* during the session count as bad.
    [ -s "$link" ] || { echo "n/a"; return; }
    awk '/scdc=unreadable/ {u++; next}
         { n++
           for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) { split($i, kv, "=")
             if (kv[1]=="clk" && kv[2]!="1") nolock++
             if (kv[1]=="lock" && kv[2]!="111") nolock++
             if (kv[1]=="scr" && kv[2]!="1") noscr++
             if (kv[1]=="err") { m = split(kv[2], e, ",")
               for (j = 1; j <= m; j++) if (e[j] ~ /^[0-9]+$/) {
                 if (n == 1) first[j] = e[j]
                 else if (e[j] > last[j]) { grew++; added += e[j] - last[j] }
                 else if (e[j] < last[j]) { grew++; added += e[j] }   # counter was cleared, new errors
                 last[j] = e[j] } } } }
         END { r = ""
               if (nolock) r = r sprintf(" unlocked:%d", nolock)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Read HDMI 2.0 link health from the TV itself (SCDC registers over DDC, read-only).
# This sees the signal *as the TV receives it*, i.e. after the cable -- unlike
# gamescope screenshots, which are clean even when the TV picture is torn.
#
#   gaming-mode-hdmi-link                 # one line: lock / scrambling / error counts
#   gaming-mode-hdmi-link watch [secs=2]  # one line per interval until killed
#   gaming-mode-hdmi-link bus             # print the i2c bus the TV is on
#
# Fields:  clk=1 lock=111  -> TMDS clock + channels 0/1/2 locked (anything else = bad)
#          scr=1           -> TV has locked onto the scrambled signal (needed at 4K60)
#          cfg=03          -> source asked for scrambling + 1/40 clock ratio
#          err=a,b,c       -> character errors per channel since last read (0 = clean)
# Needs read access to /dev/i2c-N (uaccess ACL on the active seat, or the i2c group).
connector="${GAMING_MODE_HDMI_CONNECTOR:-HDMI-A-1}"

find_bus() {   # the NVIDIA DDC bus whose EDID vendor bytes match the connector's EDID
    local edid want b
    edid=$(ls /sys/class/drm/card*-"$connector"/edid 2>/dev/null | head -1)
    [ -n "$edid" ] || return 1
    want=$(od -An -tx1 -j8 -N2 "$edid" | tr -d ' \n')
    for b in /sys/bus/i2c/devices/i2c-*/name; do
        grep -q 'NVIDIA i2c adapter\|AMDGPU DM\|i915 gmbus\|DP-AUX\|ddc' "$b" 2>/dev/null || continue
        b=${b%/name}; b=${b##*/i2c-}
        got=$( { i2cget -y "$b" 0x50 0x08 && i2cget -y "$b" 0x50 0x09; } 2>/dev/null | sed 's/0x//' | tr -d '\n')
        [ "$got" = "$want" ] && { echo "$b"; return 0; }
    done
    return 1
}

bus="${GAMING_MODE_HDMI_BUS:-}"
[ -n "$bus" ] || bus=$(find_bus) || { echo "hdmi-link: no DDC bus for $connector" >&2; exit 1; }

rd() { i2cget -y "$bus" 0x54 "$1" 2>/dev/null || echo X; }
ced() {   # ced <lo> <hi>: 15-bit count if valid bit set, else '-'
    local lo hi; lo=$(rd "$1"); hi=$(rd "$2")
    [[ $lo == X || $hi == X ]] && { echo X; return; }
    (( hi & 0x80 )) && echo $(( ((hi & 0x7f) << 8) | lo )) || echo -
}
sample() {
    local cfg scr st e0 e1 e2
    cfg=$(rd 0x20); scr=$(rd 0x21); st=$(rd 0x40)
    if [[ $st == X ]]; then echo "$(date +%T) scdc=unreadable"; return; fi
    e0=$(ced 0x50 0x51); e1=$(ced 0x52 0x53); e2=$(ced 0x54 0x55)
    printf '%s clk=%d lock=%d%d%d scr=%d cfg=%02x err=%s,%s,%s\n' "$(date +%T)" \
        $(( st & 1 )) $(( st >> 1 & 1 )) $(( st >> 2 & 1 )) $(( st >> 3 & 1 )) \
        $(( scr & 1 )) $(( cfg )) "$e0" "$e1" "$e2"
}

case "${1:-}" in
    bus)   echo "$bus" ;;
    watch) while :; do sample; sleep "${2:-2}"; done ;;
    *)     sample ;;
esac

#!/bin/sh
# Runs when Gaming Mode (gamescope-session.service) stops. Decides where the next
# login goes. While Gaming Mode runs, the login manager is left pointing at it, so:
#   - PC rebooting/shutting down -> leave it: boot comes back into Gaming Mode
#   - easy-switch screen change  -> leave it: relog straight back on the new screen
#   - anything else (crash, Steam quit, "Switch to Desktop") -> back to Plasma,
#     so a broken Gaming Mode can never loop
flag="$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/easy-switch-gamescope-restart"
if [ -e "$flag" ]; then
    rm -f "$flag"
    exit 0
fi
case "$(systemctl is-system-running 2>/dev/null)" in
    stopping) exit 0 ;;
esac
# Home Assistant's Shut down / Reboot button (ha-update poweroff|reboot) ends the
# session itself ~15 s BEFORE it calls systemctl, so the system is still "running"
# here - without this the PC came back up in the desktop (2026-11-12).
systemctl is-active --quiet ha-power.service && exit 0
exec /usr/bin/pkexec /usr/lib/steamos/steam-set-session plasma.desktop

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Strip per-game launch-option boilerplate that's now handled globally:
  - `game-performance`            -> steam-game-performance.service does it for every game
  - `PROTON_ENABLE_WAYLAND=0`     -> already the default in ~/.config/environment.d/gaming.conf
  - `gamescope ... --` wrappers   -> Gaming Mode already runs games inside gamescope
Leaves real per-game settings (e.g. -nolauncher, VKD3D_CONFIG=...) alone. A bare
`%command%` is cleared. Dry run by default; --apply writes (Steam MUST be closed).
"""
import glob, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, time
import vdf

APPLY = "--apply" in sys.argv

def clean(lo: str) -> str:
    s = re.sub(r"(^|\s)gamescope\s.*?\s--(?=\s)", r"\1", lo)   # gamescope <args> --
    s = re.sub(r"(^|\s)game-performance(?=\s|$)", r"\1", s)
    s = re.sub(r"(^|\s)PROTON_ENABLE_WAYLAND=0(?=\s|$)", r"\1", s)
    s = " ".join(s.split())
    return "" if s == "%command%" else s

if APPLY and subprocess.run(["pgrep", "-x", "steam"], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL).returncode == 0:
    sys.exit("Steam is running. Close it (Steam menu -> Exit) and try again.")

for path in glob.glob(os.path.expanduser("~/.steam/steam/userdata/*/config/localconfig.vdf")):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        cfg = vdf.load(f)
    apps = cfg["UserLocalConfigStore"]["Software"]["Valve"]["Steam"]["apps"]
    cleared = kept = 0
    for aid, app in apps.items():
        if not isinstance(app, dict) or not app.get("LaunchOptions"):
            continue
        old = app["LaunchOptions"]; new = clean(old)
        if new == old:
            continue
        if new:
            print(f"  {aid:>8}: {old!r}\n  {'':>8}  -> {new!r}")
            kept += 1
        else:
            cleared += 1
        if APPLY:
            if new: app["LaunchOptions"] = new
            else: del app["LaunchOptions"]
    print(f"{path}: {cleared} cleared to empty, {kept} trimmed (shown above)")
    if APPLY:
        backup = f"{path}.bak-{time.strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}"
        shutil.copy2(path, backup)
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            vdf.dump(cfg, f, pretty=True)
        print(f"written (backup: {backup})")
if not APPLY:
    print("dry run -- re-run with --apply while Steam is closed")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Automatic CachyOS game-performance for every Steam game, no launch options needed.
# While any Steam game is running (Steam's "reaper SteamLaunch AppId=..." process),
# hold the performance power profile and block idle/sleep -- the same thing
# `game-performance %command%` does per game. Released when the last game exits.
hold=
release() { [ -n "$hold" ] && kill "$hold" 2>/dev/null; hold=; }
trap 'release; exit 0' TERM INT

while true; do
    if pgrep -f 'reaper SteamLaunch AppId=' >/dev/null; then
        if [ -z "$hold" ] || ! kill -0 "$hold" 2>/dev/null; then
            systemd-inhibit --why "Steam game running" \
                powerprofilesctl launch -p performance -r "Steam game running" -- sleep infinity &
            hold=$!
            echo "game started: holding performance profile"
        fi
    elif [ -n "$hold" ]; then
        release
        echo "no games running: released performance profile"
    fi
    sleep 3
done

#!/bin/sh
# Gaming Mode on NVIDIA: always composite in gamescope instead of handing
# separate layers / direct scan-out to the driver. Without this the TV showed
# torn, offset, miscoloured blocks (Steam UI and game layers mis-merged).
# Put first in PATH by the gamescope-session.service drop-in.
# Extra flags for testing: one line in ~/.config/gaming-mode/extra-args
# (set with `gaming-mode-extra-args`), inserted before the session's own args.
# Wrapper-only pseudo-flags (not passed to gamescope):
#   --x-explicit-sync        leave gamescope's explicit sync ON this start, i.e. disable
#                            ~/.config/gamescope/scripts/50-nvidia-tv-fix.lua (renamed .off)
#   --x-convar NAME=VALUE    set a gamescope convar this start (via 60-gaming-mode-test.lua)
#   --x-bin PATH             run this gamescope binary instead of /usr/bin/gamescope
cfg="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}"
scripts="$cfg/gamescope/scripts"
lua="$scripts/50-nvidia-tv-fix.lua"
test_lua="$scripts/60-gaming-mode-test.lua"
rm -f "$test_lua"
explicit=0; pass=""
# GBM scan-out build (fixes NVIDIA 4K scan-out corruption, see GAMING-MODE.md) if present,
# else the system gamescope. Delete ~/.local/opt/gamescope-gbm to go back to stock.
bin=/usr/bin/gamescope
[ -x "$HOME/.local/opt/gamescope-gbm/gamescope" ] && bin="$HOME/.local/opt/gamescope-gbm/gamescope"
# shellcheck disable=SC2046
set -- $(head -1 "$cfg/gaming-mode/extra-args" 2>/dev/null) -- "$@"
while [ "$1" != "--" ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --x-explicit-sync) explicit=1 ;;
        --x-bin) shift; [ -x "$1" ] && bin=$1 || echo "wrapper: --x-bin $1 not executable, using $bin" >&2 ;;
        --x-convar)
            shift; name=${1%%=*}; val=${1#*=}
            case "$name" in *[!a-z0-9_]*|"") echo "wrapper: bad convar $1" >&2; shift; continue ;; esac
            case "$val" in true|false|[0-9]*) ;; *) val="\"$val\"" ;; esac
            mkdir -p "$scripts"
            printf 'gamescope.convars.%s.value = %s\n(warn or print)("60-gaming-mode-test: %s = " .. tostring(gamescope.convars.%s.value))\n' \
                "$name" "$val" "$name" "$name" >> "$test_lua" ;;
        *) pass="$pass $1" ;;
    esac
    shift
done
shift   # drop the "--" separator; "$@" is now the session's own arguments
if [ "$explicit" = 1 ]; then [ -e "$lua" ] && mv -f "$lua" "$lua.off"
else [ -e "$lua.off" ] && mv -f "$lua.off" "$lua"; fi
# shellcheck disable=SC2086  # word-splitting of $pass is intended
exec "$bin" --force-composition $pass "$@"
